provenance: Seed list written from general knowledge; every entry is unverified against a source (source_verified=false). No collection is claimed to be fully catalogued.

excluded.title: Chacha Chaudhary (and related characters)
excluded.reason: Copyrighted comic franchise. Not reproduced. The library offers only original archetypes (e.g. the Scholar, Elderly Man, Villager) that carry no franchise designs.

collections.name: Panchatantra
collections.origin: Ancient Sanskrit animal-fable collection (attributed to Vishnu Sharma); many recensions and translations.
collections.public_domain_note: Underlying tales are traditional; specific translations may be copyrighted.

stories.premise: A monkey outwits a crocodile who wants his heart.
A jackal dyed blue passes as a king until he howls.

stories.title_en: The Lion and the Clever Rabbit
stories.premise: A rabbit tricks a tyrant lion into a well.

stories.title_en: The Crows and the Black Snake
stories.premise: Crows get rid of a snake by using a queen's necklace.
A talkative tortoise falls while being carried by geese.

stories.title_en: The Brahmin's Wife and the Mongoose
stories.premise: A hasty act wrongs a faithful mongoose.
A curious monkey pulls a wedge from a half-split log.
A cunning crane is outwitted by a crab.

stories.title_en: The Merchant and the Mice that Ate Iron
stories.premise: A merchant answers a lie with a bigger tale.

stories.title_en: The Donkey in the Tiger's Skin
stories.premise: A washerman's donkey is caught by its bray.
A crow, mouse, tortoise and deer help each other.
A lion is turned against his bull friend by a jackal.

stories.title_en: The War of the Crows and the Owls
stories.premise: A crow feigns exile to destroy the owls.
Small friends bring down a proud elephant.

collections.name: Jataka tales
collections.origin: Buddhist birth-story tradition in Pali; many retellings.

stories.premise: A monkey king makes a bridge of his body to save his troop.
A golden deer offers its life for a doe.
A hare gives all it has to a hungry stranger.
A deer king asks to be taken in place of a doe.
A swan with golden feathers is betrayed by greed.

collections.name: Hitopadesha
collections.origin: Sanskrit fable collection (Narayana Pandit), related to the Panchatantra.

stories.premise: A crow, mouse, tortoise and deer form a friendship.

stories.title_en: The Tiger and the Traveller with the Gold Bracelet
stories.premise: A greedy traveller is deceived by an old tiger.
A hare ends a lion's tyranny with a reflection.

stories.title_en: Vikram and Betal: the frame story
stories.premise: King Vikram carries the vetala from the tree in the burning ground; it tells riddles on the way.

stories.title_en: Vikram and Betal: the three suitors
stories.premise: A riddle about who deserves a princess.

collections.name: Singhasan Battisi
collections.origin: Frame-story of 32 tales told by statues on King Vikramaditya's throne.

stories.title_en: Singhasan Battisi: the throne of Vikramaditya
stories.premise: King Bhoj finds a throne guarded by 32 statues who each tell a tale of Vikramaditya.

collections.name: Akbar and Birbal
collections.origin: Folk tradition of court anecdotes; mostly legendary rather than historical.
collections.public_domain_note: Traditional; modern books may be copyrighted.

stories.premise: Birbal shows the emperor that real warmth cannot come from afar.
Birbal answers a trick question with an exact-sounding reply.

stories.title_en: The Longer and the Shorter Line
stories.premise: Birbal makes a line shorter by drawing a longer one next to it.

collections.name: Tenali Raman
collections.origin: Folk tradition of court wit attributed to a poet at the Vijayanagara court.
collections.public_domain_note: Traditional; modern books may be copyrighted.

stories.title_en: Tenali Raman and the Cat's Milk
stories.premise: Tenali proves a point about royal gifts with hot milk and a cat.
Tenali turns thieves' own labour into digging his garden.

stories.title_en: Tenali Raman and the Brinjal Curry
stories.premise: A courtier's praise of brinjal is tested.

collections.name: Aesop's fables
collections.public_domain_note: Traditional and widely in the public domain; check the translation used.

stories.premise: A steady tortoise beats a boastful hare.
A fox calls grapes sour when it cannot reach them.
A mouse repays a lion's mercy.
A shepherd boy's false alarms leave him unheard.
A crow raises water in a pot with pebbles.
A summer of play leaves the grasshopper hungry in winter.

stories.title_en: The Goose that Laid the Golden Eggs
stories.premise: Greed kills the source of wealth.

collections.name: Arabian Nights (One Thousand and One Nights)
collections.origin: Middle-Eastern and South-Asian frame-story collection; some well-known tales (e.g. Aladdin) were added by later translators.
collections.public_domain_note: Older translations are in the public domain; check the one used.

stories.premise: A merchant's seven voyages.
A fisherman releases a jinni from a jar.

stories.title_en: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
stories.premise: A woodcutter finds a robbers' treasure cave.
A boy and a genie in a lamp. (A later addition to the collection.)

collections.name: Regional folk tales
collections.origin: Not catalogued: no regional tale is listed until its source is verified.

stories.title_en: The Farmer and the Rich Man
stories.premise: Project-original story.
